The producer's operative words for 5 CFR 6.6 are not EO 11315's. EO 13562 sec. 7(a)(iv) (75 FR 82587-88, 2010) rewrote the first sentence of 6.6 'to read' 'OPM may remove any position from or may revoke in whole or in part any provision of Schedule A, B, C, or D.' EO 12043 sec. 2 (1978) deleted 11315's second sentence ('These changes are effective on publication in the Federal Register') and substituted the present notice sentence. Nothing of 11315's 1966 text of 6.6 remains in force.
Sec. 2(a) (6.1(a)): third sentence deleted by EO 12043 sec. 1; 6.1(a) rewritten 'to read' by EO 13562 sec. 7(a)(i); further amended 91 FR 52479 (2026).

Sec. 1 (Rule IX) revoked by EO 12748 sec. 8(a) (re-fetched, APP). The YES bridge fails TC05/TC08. 1-101 (revocation of the prohibitions of EO 12205, EO 12211, Proc. 4702) is a spent dispositive act (TC07). 1-102 delegates IEEPA functions only 'to carry out the purpose of this Order', i.e. the 1981 lifting; no current Part 535 provision implements that lifting (eCFR Part 535 read: operative sections implement the EO 12170 blocking and the Algiers-Accords orders 12276-12281/12294, each with its own delegation).

The 91 FR 61730 authority line (2026-09-30) is a cumulative bundle of every Iran-crisis order. It also lists EO 12205 and EO 12211, whose prohibitions EO 12282 itself revoked in 1981, so listing in the line is not evidence that a listed order still operates (counterexample, TC16). The same bundle appears in every OFAC penalty-inflation rule 1996-2025 (FR search: 21 hits, all Part 535 authority lines). The 2026 rule only moved penalty text; it gives no clause-level reliance on 12282.
